# AI agent lens 0.1.0

The criteria a design adds when any element is an agent: a model that chooses its own steps, calls tools, keeps memory and acts in the world. An agent is a service with an ai facet and an agent facet, so the core and AI solution lenses apply to it too. This lens asks what changes when the design's behaviour is chosen at run time: whether agency is justified, whether every action is inventoried and bounded where the agent cannot change the bound, whether injected instructions can reach a consequential action, and whether the agent can be watched, stopped and held to account. It carries the bundle's own agent-native rules (guardrail tiers, capability scope, provenance) into an assessment.

Applies to designs with the `ai-agent` profile. Source: [`standards/assessment/lenses/ai-agent.yaml`](../../standards/assessment/lenses/ai-agent.yaml).

## JUS: Justified agency

Is an agent needed, at the autonomy it is given?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AGT-JUS-01](agt-jus-01.md) | Does the design justify an agent over a workflow, and a multi-agent topology over a single agent? | major | reviewer |
| [AGT-JUS-02](agt-jus-02.md) | Is the autonomy level declared and proportionate to the impact and reversibility of what the agent does? | blocker | both |

## ACT: Actions and blast radius

Is every action inventoried, tiered, and bounded outside the agent's reach?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AGT-ACT-01](agt-act-01.md) | Is every action the agent can take in the world listed, with its effect and whether it can be undone? | blocker | both |
| [AGT-ACT-02](agt-act-02.md) | Do irreversible, financial, destructive and external-communication actions need human approval, or sit behind a T0 or T1 limit? | blocker | tool |
| [AGT-ACT-03](agt-act-03.md) | Are T0 and T1 limits enforced outside anything the agent can edit? | blocker | tool |
| [AGT-ACT-04](agt-act-04.md) | Is code the agent generates or runs executed in a sandbox with no standing credentials? | blocker | both |

## INJ: Injection and trust

Can untrusted content steer the agent into a consequential action?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AGT-INJ-01](agt-inj-01.md) | Does any single agent session combine untrusted input, access to sensitive data and the ability to change state or communicate externally? | blocker | tool |
| [AGT-INJ-02](agt-inj-02.md) | Does the design use a pattern that limits what injected instructions can do, rather than relying on the model to refuse them? | major | both |
| [AGT-INJ-03](agt-inj-03.md) | Is the agent's goal fixed by its principal and protected from being rewritten by content it reads? | major | reviewer |

## ID: Identity and privilege

Does the agent act as itself, with only the privilege its task needs?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AGT-ID-01](agt-id-01.md) | Does the agent have its own workload identity, and is it clear whether it acts as itself or on behalf of a user? | blocker | tool |
| [AGT-ID-02](agt-id-02.md) | Is every tool credential scoped to the task, and never broader than the user it acts for? | major | both |
| [AGT-ID-03](agt-id-03.md) | Do MCP and other tool servers validate token audience and refuse to pass tokens through? | major | reviewer |

## MEM: Memory and context

Can what the agent remembers be poisoned or leak across users?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AGT-MEM-01](agt-mem-01.md) | Can untrusted content be written to long-term memory, and if so, is it validated and attributed? | major | both |
| [AGT-MEM-02](agt-mem-02.md) | Is memory isolated per user or tenant, with stated retention? | major | tool |

## MAS: Multi-agent and supply chain

Are peers, tools and protocols authenticated, pinned and contained?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AGT-MAS-01](agt-mas-01.md) | Is every agent-to-agent interaction authenticated, with the peer's trust stated? | blocker | tool |
| [AGT-MAS-02](agt-mas-02.md) | Is a failure or compromise in one agent contained, so it cannot cascade through the others? | major | both |
| [AGT-MAS-03](agt-mas-03.md) | Are tools, MCP servers, agent cards and protocol versions pinned and from trusted sources? | major | both |

## CTL: Control and accountability

Can the agent be watched, limited, stopped and held to account?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AGT-CTL-01](agt-ctl-01.md) | Are step, cost and time limits set, and is there a kill switch that works without the agent's cooperation? | blocker | tool |
| [AGT-CTL-02](agt-ctl-02.md) | Is every plan, tool call and output recorded with provenance, so an action can be traced to the input that caused it? | major | tool |
| [AGT-CTL-03](agt-ctl-03.md) | Is human approval protected from manipulation and from automation bias? | major | reviewer |
| [AGT-CTL-04](agt-ctl-04.md) | Is drift between what the agent did and what policy intended reconciled continuously, and is a rogue agent detectable? | major | reviewer |

## EVAL: Evaluating behaviour

Is the agent evaluated on what it does, repeatedly, not only on what it ends with?

| Criterion | Question | Severity | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|
| [AGT-EVAL-01](agt-eval-01.md) | Is the agent evaluated on its trajectory, not only its final output? | major | tool |
| [AGT-EVAL-02](agt-eval-02.md) | Is reliability measured over repeated runs, and is the agent tested against injection and hijacking? | major | both |
